paragraphs: Mentioned at the beginning of Nazir, chapter 7, and in Semachot, chapter 4, halakhah 28, where he is described as a Kohen.[^1][^2]

notes.text: רפ״ז gives beginning of Nazir chapter 7, not end. שמחות פ״ד ה״כח explicitly gives Semachot chapter 4 halakhah 28, while earlier machine ה״כה gives 25. No named edition is independently checked.

פכסס retains both samekhs as Pakhsas, not the older Pakhas. There is read contextually as the second cited source Semachot; its Kohen statement remains Hyman’s report, not an identity or priesthood admission. The heading has no added title.
